claim_comment: Validating the canonical provider handshake after the capability authority landed: protocol negotiation must fail closed before mutation, finite limits must cover transport and execution, and implementation/state identity must stay immutable for one retained instance.
acceptance_criteria: Incompatible providers fail with a typed terminal outcome.
Limits cover payload size, concurrency, queueing, and supported scopes.
Build/state identity is immutable for a running provider instance.
close_reason: Accepted the canonical V1 provider handshake with fail-closed version negotiation, finite scoped limits, typed terminal outcomes, and immutable implementation/state identity for each retained instance.
close_comment: Evidence: product/contracts/memory-provider-v1/provider-handshake-contract.json plus its strict JSON Schema define the only V1 handshake request, response, protocol, exact-scope, identity, limits, readiness and receipt authority. Compatibility selects one accepted registration and exact protocol intersection before any state mutation; provider, adapter, protocol, challenge, state owner/schema/namespace/scope, capabilities and limits each fail to deterministic typed non-ready states. Eight bounded limit dimensions cover request/response payloads, observation batches, recall candidates, concurrent operations, operation duration, snapshots and inspection; exact supported scope is separately mandatory and wildcard/CWD inference is forbidden. Implementation build/artifact identity and provider state namespace/schema/scope/generation are independently digested into an expiring ready receipt that cannot survive provider restart, registration revision, or scope revision. Tests and the repository checker enforce read-only handshake, deadline/cancellation propagation, no fake readiness and no silent fallback.
